To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unregistered practitioners in urban China are not an isolated phenomenon but a result of the interaction of several factors and processes in the health care system and the society at large.
unregistered practitioners have a significant role in the urban Chinese health care system.
the development and the prevalence of unregistered practitioners in China is the result of a complex interplay of structural, institutional and cultural factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ambivalent role of unregistered practitioners in China's health care system.
the role of unregistered practitioners in the health care provision system of urban China.
the role of unregistered practitioners for health care disparities and health governance in the context of urbanisation in China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unregistered practitioners are not only a result of the health care reform, but also a consequence of the general development in the Chinese health governance system.
unregistered practitioners are a necessary but not sufficient condition for the provision of adequate health care to marginalised populations in urban China.
, on the one hand, unregistered practitioners are a symptom of a dysfunctional health care system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the role of unregistered practitioners is ambivalent: on the one hand they provide health care services that are not available in the formal system, on the other hand they undermine the legitimacy of formal health care institutions and the state.
unregistered practitioners are a result of health system deficiencies, but they are not the solution to these problems.
unregistered practitioners are a symptom of a dysfunctional health care system and a challenge for its governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unregistered providers are a major source of health care provision for rural-to-urban migrant workers and that they are perceived as more trustworthy, more accessible and less expensive.
the role of unregistered practitioners in China is ambivalent.

unregistered practitioners are an ambivalent phenomenon: On the one hand, they can be a means to improve access and affordability of health care, on the other hand, they can contribute to the further fragmentation of the health care system and to the erosion of the public health system.
